justicia_brandegeeana.why: dense glossy shrub from Weeping Fig leaves, reads as a leafy shrub at 5 m and 15 m; still a tidy egg where the real plant is lax and arching, and bracts are absent (no scan)
justicia_brandegeeana.reference_photo: Wikimedia Commons 'Justicia brandegeeana 2020 Walbrzych kz01' (CC BY-SA 4.0); used for grading only, not committed

salvia_leucantha.why: narrow-leaf mound but the plant is a round dome of olive-yellow leaves on visible trunks; real S. leucantha is an upright mass of grey-green velvety lance leaves whose identity is the purple spikes (no scan, none invented). The Australian Laurel scan colours drift yellow under the grey-green tint (hue gain clipped, blue channel near zero)
salvia_leucantha.reference_photo: Wikimedia Commons 'Salvia leucantha (Mexican Bush Sage)' (CC BY-SA 4.0); used for grading only, not committed

acorus_gramineus.why: African Flag blades: reads as an ornamental grass clump at 5 m and a small tuft at 15 m; sparser and straighter than the dense, finely arching Acorus fans
acorus_gramineus.reference_photo: Wikimedia Commons 'Acorus gramineus' (CC BY 2.0); used for grading only, not committed

alpinia_zerumbet.why: unchanged: leafy canes with lanceolate leaves, reads as a ginger; narrower, more upright and less glossy than the reference; not in the layout
alpinia_zerumbet.reference_photo: Wikimedia Commons 'Alpinia zerumbet - shell ginger' (CC BY-SA 4.0); used for grading only, not committed

farfugium_japonicum.why: the Elephant Ear scan (a pointed sagittate Alocasia leaf) was tried and rejected: wrong leaf shape; the Taro bank is kept. Even so a sparse tall plant on bare petioles; the real farfugium is a dense low mound of round to kidney leaves, so it fails the reference comparison (it was B by the sourced-habit-text check)
farfugium_japonicum.reference_photo: Wikimedia Commons 'Farfugium japonicum kz01' (CC BY-SA 4.0); used for grading only, not committed

fatsia_japonica.why: unchanged. The Tree Philodendron leaf was tried (sheet rendered, not kept): its leaf is narrow and pinnatifid, the plant reads as a lanky philodendron, not Fatsia. The generated 9-lobe palmate outline reads as Fatsia; lower stems are bare
fatsia_japonica.reference_photo: Wikimedia Commons 'Fatsia japonica kz03' (CC BY-SA 4.0); used for grading only, not committed

jasminum_sambac.why: wisteria leaflets as a dense glossy climber panel with trailing shoots, reads as a climber at 5/15 m; leaves are smaller and more pointed than the broad round leaves of Arabian jasmine, no flowers (no scan)
jasminum_sambac.reference_photo: Wikimedia Commons 'Jasminum sambac kz01' (CC BY-SA 4.0); used for grading only, not committed

trachelospermum_jasminoides.why: unchanged: the species-faithful plant; compact uniform leaf wall, no flowers
trachelospermum_jasminoides.reference_photo: Wikimedia Commons 'Trachelospermum jasminoides Reunion' (CC0); used for grading only, not committed

petrea_volubilis.why: wisteria leaflets on a lax climber: reads as a leafy climber but not as Petrea; the genus is defined by violet-blue calyx racemes at 5 m and 15 m, and no scan of them exists, so none were invented. Leaves are smaller and more pointed than Petrea's rough oblong-elliptic leaves
petrea_volubilis.reference_photo: Wikimedia Commons 'Petrea volubilis bush' (CC BY-SA 3.0); used for grading only, not committed

vitis_vinifera.why: lobed Common Grape Vine scan leaves (species fidelity), a lax vine with open gaps, visible canes and hanging shoots; reads as a grape on a trellis at 5 m, a green mass at 15 m. Compared with the reference the leaves are darker and the habit still too compact; no tendrils or bunches (the atlas holds only tendril-bearing sprigs, not usable tendril or fruit cut-outs, so none were invented)
vitis_vinifera.reference_photo: Wikimedia Commons 'Common grape vine (Vitis vinifera) leaves intertwined with a wire fence' (CC BY-SA 4.0); used for grading only, not committed

lagerstroemia_indica.why: multi-stem tree with pale grey-tan Banyan Bark; reads as crape myrtle at 5/15 m; leaf-off is stronger; no panicles (no scan), leaves are star-jasmine leaves (form-class)
lagerstroemia_indica.reference_photo: Wikimedia Commons 'Lagerstroemia indica MHNT Jardin des Plantes de Toulouse' (CC BY-SA 4.0); used for grading only, not committed

pittosporum_tobira.why: new class: dense glossy mounded shrub from the Australian Laurel scan (genus match, form-class); reads as Pittosporum at 5 m and 15 m; the real plant's leaf whorls are more clustered at the tips and fruit/flowers are absent
pittosporum_tobira.reference_photo: Wikimedia Commons 'Pittosporum-tobira-Sitia-Crete-Greece' (CC BY-SA 4.0); used for grading only, not committed
